title: SUPeR-Seq
scope: Original SUPeR-Seq implementation for linear and circular RNA transcript profiling, at the assigned Illumina schematic level: single-cell RNA through purified amplified cDNA. The two RNA drawings represent poly(A)+ and non-poly(A) molecular classes within a single preparation; no isolated fractions or pooling are established. The SUPeR-seq rows in the two poster images corroborate the assigned target. Neighboring scRNA-seq, MATQ-seq, UMI Method rows and adjacent chemical structures are outside this extraction. Primary-paper evidence resolves primer identity, cDNA-tailing order, and the DNA endpoint. Subsequent TruSeq preparation, sequencing and junction analysis explain that endpoint’s use without adding unshown graph operations.

operations.label: Synthesize first-strand cDNA and digest excess primers
operations.description: Copy the RNA into first-strand cDNA, then digest unreacted primers using ExoSAP-IT to reduce primer-dimer formation.
operations.mechanism: SuperScript III reverse transcriptase copies RNA primed by AnchorX-T15N6; excess primers are digested after first-strand synthesis.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is represented by copied cDNA. A circular RNA template can contribute sequence without making the cDNA a circular RNA molecule. Recovery is incomplete: the paper reports that a single-cell SUPeR-seq sample recovered only a subset of the poly(A)- genes identified in bulk RNA sequencing.

operations.label: Polyadenylate first-strand cDNA and synthesize the second strand
operations.description: Add a poly(A) tract to the 3′ end of newly synthesized cDNA, then synthesize a complementary DNA strand using AnchorY-T24. These steps resolve the broad RT block’s A/T-containing DNA interface.
operations.mechanism: TdT uses dATP with ddATP to limit poly(A)-tail extension; AnchorY-T24 primes the second strand from the added tract.
operations.information_effect: The artificial tail is an amplification interface on DNA. It does not indicate that the source RNA had a native poly(A) tail. Different anchors support subsequent PCR.

operations.information_effect: The endpoint is physical RNA-derived DNA, ready for subsequent TruSeq DNA library preparation. Later sequencing can profile linear transcripts and identify candidate circRNAs through junction-spanning reads and circular exon order. Circular topology is inferred from sequence organization, not retained as an RNA circle in this product; junction evidence is required, so ordinary host-gene reads alone do not identify a circRNA. Sequencing and computation are outside the depicted graph.

method_scopes.rationale: The card and both poster rows identify this single target. The original Fan et al. paper explicitly describes SUPeR-seq random priming, first-strand cDNA/primer digestion, cDNA tailing/second-strand synthesis, PCR and purification. Both illustrated RNA classes are eligible in the same single-cell reaction, including circRNA among non-polyadenylated RNA. The second-strand interface is resolved from the primary paper within the schematic’s broad RT block. No separate biological methods or target workflows are inferred from the neighboring poster rows. Circular topology is represented as a paper-supported subpopulation of the non-poly(A) material, without adding a separately routed circle-enrichment workflow.
